newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Sep 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Sep 25.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO DAILY NEWS -- Political tensions between China, Japan and the United States over the disputed islands in the East China Sea are increasing.
-- Revolutionary musicals and ballets are making a comeback in China.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- China accused Japan of invading the disputed islands in the East China Sea, and demanded it withdraw its presence there.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The Civil Aviation Administration of China indicated that some airlines would be opened to foreign investment.
-- Trade specialists dismissed fears that a big increase in Hong Kong's overseas investment signalled a flight of capital before the 1997 handover.
-- The best retail sales figures in five months were greeted with caution by retailers, economists and bankers who warned the 18-month slump might not be over.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Hong Kong's flag carrier, Cathay Pacific, urged the government to consider the regional competitiveness of the new Chek Lap Kok airport when deciding the index of landing and taking-off fees.
-- ORIENTAL DAILY NEWS -- Governor Chris Patten ordered an inquiry into the conduct of a High Court judge.
-- A mainland immigrant to Hong Kong was suspected to have killed his family by turning his flat into a gas chamber.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- The Monetary Authority was considering setting up a central credit information bank to provide information on credit card applicants to local banks.
